items.english: Taki had been thinking of nothing but his creative work, his novel, until it turned oppressive, so he took up his sketch box and went out for a walk — down the stone steps and on wavering down toward the pine wood near the sea. More mindful of passersby than of the view, he left the path and, bending low, hid himself in a thicket of dwarf pines that caught at his head. Then, coming to the broken edge of the hill, he sat cross-legged among the evening primroses. Far off on the sand that shone grey, four or five things like cloths toyed with by the wind were turning in slow circles, and wondering what they could be, he looked up and saw they were the shadows of gulls wheeling low in great rings.
notes: Kept the single long movement of hiding, sitting, and mistaking shadows; evening primrose for 月見草.

items.english: On the hot evening of the second, having finished his board of the distant sea, Taki was trailing blankly home when near the foot of the stone steps he met his wife, who seemed to have been wandering about looking for him.
"Have you just got here? Have you come to visit?"
notes: Taken as Taki to his wife, from the meeting in p3.

items.english: "I've come to watch them catch the scarlet carp, but they say they just can't catch them!"
notes: Hi-goi kept as scarlet carp; catch kept plain for the tolling verb.

items.english: "Again... You had better give it up. In the first place, even if you moved them to a pond like that, they would make no show, they would only stink miserably."
"But wasn't it dug on purpose for them? They say it is small but quite deep, so it will be all right!"
"They say that hole was dug because they needed the earth somewhere and had no choice — there seem to be a few goldfish and cheap carp in it, but I think that is just about right."
notes: Cheap carp for 駄鯉, to keep the low value against the later valuation.

data.say: Drafted the opening walk and the first carp exchange.
